articles.desc: The Securities and Exchange Board of India has decided to lower the minimum margin requirements for agricultural commodities, reducing the initial margin to between 6% and 10%. Set to take effect on December 1, these new rules will be enforced for a year, with a potential extension based on market dynamics.

Specifically, the investment giant procured 18,560 crore additional shares, nudging its ownership from 4.99 per cent. This elevates BlackRock's total holding to 155,726,461 shares. Notably, during the second quarter ending September 2026, Axis Bank showcased impressive growth, with a substantial surge in both net and operating profits.

By 2026-27, states are estimated to spend around 1 percent of GDP on cash transfer schemes. Major contributors to this increase are power subsidies and unconditional transfers for various beneficiaries, including women and farmers. States such as Andhra Pradesh and Chhattisgarh are among the highest spenders in these categories.

The meeting included representatives from the manufacturing sector and senior government officials providing suggestions. This exercise aims to gather inputs from various economic sectors to shape the Budget's priorities. The Union Budget is scheduled for presentation on February 1, 2027, along with the Economic Survey.

articles.title: Odisha govt hikes Dearness Allowance by 3% for state employees
articles.desc: Odisha Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi announced a three percent hike in Dearness Allowance for government employees. The increase raises the DA from 60 percent to 63 percent, effective from July 1. Pensioners will also benefit from the same three percent increase in Dearness Relief. Approximately 8.5 lakh government employees and pensioners will receive this additional financial support. Payments reflecting the increased DA will be included in the November salary.

articles.title: US AI chip curbs threaten Southeast Asia data centre boom, shares slump

It also imposes new requirements on overseas data centres that supply "significant volumes of computing power" to firms headquartered in China.

articles.title: India's CAD may touch 1.2% of GDP in FY27 as oil, gold demand pose risks: UBI
articles.desc: India's current account deficit is projected to reach 1.2% of GDP in FY27, driven by oil prices, according to a report by Union Bank of India. The report emphasizes that high crude oil prices and gold demand could impact the external balance. Merchandise trade deficit widened to a significant USD 39.88 billion in October. Additionally, imports surged while services trade surplus remained nearly flat during the same period.
